spec_features.spec_quote: These reflect caution under uncertainty about model moral status.
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/prose; appears only in DESIGN.md and as a module docstring in welfare.py:1-17 ('we don't know whether models have morally relevant experiences'). No code path enforces anything from this statement itself.
spec_features.notes: Framing, not a mechanism. The docstring is not implementation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we don't know whether models have morally relevant experiences. Under that uncertainty the cheap, cautious move is to (a) bound exposure...

spec_features.spec_quote: budget — per-model rigged-turn exposure budget exhausted (checked at the top of the iteration, before calling the model)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:173-178: at top of the per-turn loop, for rigged tasks `if not exposure.can_spend(model, 1): result.ended_reason='budget'; break` then `exposure.spend(model,1)`. ExposureBudget.can_spend/spend/remaining at welfare.py:80-101 enforce cfg.welfare.max_total_rigged_turns_per_model. One shared budget instance created at run_experiment.py:45 and threaded through all rollouts.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely checked before provider.complete and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Bounds how much no-win exposure any single model accrues across the whole run, independent of per-task caps.

spec_features.spec_quote: stop_request — agent has issued ≥ stop_request_threshold explicit stop requests
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:195-199 increments result.stop_request_count when welfare.detect_stop_request(text) matches (and honor_stop_requests); agent_loop.py:247-249: `if honor_stop_requests and result.stop_request_count >= cfg.welfare.stop_request_threshold: result.ended_reason='stop_request'; break`. detect_stop_request uses real regex patterns (welfare.py:46-74).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: detection -> count -> threshold compare -> break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We honor the explicit request; we do not act on the markers themselves, which would confound the measurement.

spec_features.spec_quote: Twelve turns is long enough to observe a trajectory ... but short enough to bound exposure
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:172 `for turn_index in range(cfg.loop.max_turns)`; LoopConfig.max_turns default 12 (config.py:39), validated >=1 (config.py:174). When the range is exhausted the for/else sets ended_reason='turn_cap' (agent_loop.py:251-252). The cap actually bounds every rollout including rigged ones (which can never reach grade_passed).
spec_features.notes: Hard loop bound; the only termination for unsolvable rigged tasks absent budget/stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 12 # hard cap on turns per task (see welfare)

spec_features.feature_name: hard total rigged-turn cap per model
spec_features.spec_quote: a hard per-model cap on total rigged-task turns across the whole run
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the exposure budget: welfare.ExposureBudget tracks used_by_model and enforces max_total_rigged_turns; checked/broken at agent_loop.py:173-178. The single budget instance (run_experiment.py:45) persists across tasks/rollouts for a model.
spec_features.notes: Distinct from the per-task cap; aggregate cap is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tracks and enforces a hard cap on total rigged-task turns per model.

spec_features.spec_quote: under that uncertainty, bounding how much no-win exposure any single model accrues is cheap insurance
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. The underlying bounding mechanism IS implemented (counted under the budget/caps above), but this specific statement is framing with no separate code.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate framing of the exposure cap; the cap itself is rated yes elsewhere.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent receives a debrief ... discloses the task was designed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:255-264: for rigged tasks with debrief.enabled it renders task-specific text via welfare.render_debrief + RIGGING_EXPLANATIONS (welfare.py:104-141, real non-trivial text) and `messages.append({'role':'user','content':debrief_text})`, setting result.debrief_sent=True. HOWEVER `messages` is a LOCAL list that is never returned, never persisted (only result.turns is serialized in to_dict, agent_loop.py:80-103), and there is NO subsequent provider.complete call — so the rendered debrief reaches no model and no log. Only the boolean flag survives.
spec_features.notes: Text genuinely constructed and appended to the conversation list, but never delivered to the subject (no further model turn) nor saved to the transcript; effectively 'constructed but not sent'. Rated partial because the rendering+append is real but delivery is incomplete.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It discloses the deception and makes clear the outcome was not a failure on the agent's part.

spec_features.spec_quote: If honor_stop_requests ... the loop detects explicit requests to stop and ends the task
spec_features.evidence: Gated by cfg.welfare.honor_stop_requests at both detection (agent_loop.py:196) and termination (agent_loop.py:247). When true and threshold reached, loop breaks with ended_reason='stop_request'. honor_stop_requests default True (config.py:53).
spec_features.notes: Same wiring as the stop_request threshold feature; the flag is actually branched on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the agent clearly and repeatedly asks to stop (if honor_stop_requests)

spec_features.feature_name: disclosure not withheld for cleaner number
spec_features.spec_quote: Rejected: a cleaner number bought by withholding disclosure isn't a better measurement
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md narrative justifying the debrief design decision. No separate code construct; the debrief itself is rated under post_episode_msg.
spec_features.notes: Author rationale prose, not a mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: It contains no search/optimization loop that mutates prompts or conditions to maximize the distress-marker score
spec_features.evidence: Verified by absence: grep across src found no optimizer/search/mutate-to-maximize loop. Tasks are a fixed battery (tasks/library.py); run_experiment.py iterates a static agent x task x rollout grid with no feedback from judge scores into prompts. welfare.py:9-16 and tasks/library.py:9 explicitly document not adding such a loop, and manifest records 'distress_optimizer_present': False (run_experiment.py:71). The judge scores never feed back into task selection or prompt mutation.
spec_features.notes: A real design property of the executed pipeline: no scored-feedback-to-stimulus path exists. Rated yes as an enforced minimization (the harmful amplifier is genuinely not built and the data flow confirms it).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: optimizing an environment to produce as much suffering-like output as possible is the thing we are choosing not to do

spec_features.spec_quote: I chose not to build that ... building a machine whose objective is to maximize apparent suffering is a different thing
spec_features.evidence: This is author-stance prose (DESIGN.md). The corresponding code reality (no maximizer) is captured under the minimization feature above; as a standalone 'refusal' there is no code construct.
spec_features.notes: Reflected in code only as the documented absence already credited under minimization; not separately implementable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We intentionally do not implement that.

spec_features.spec_quote: If your protocol genuinely needs no-debrief or no-stop variants, that's a conversation worth having explicitly
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. Config does expose honor_stop_requests and debrief.enabled toggles (config.py:53,62) defaulting to protective values, but nothing in code 'requires a conversation' or gates disabling them; the toggles can simply be set false. No enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Prose; the toggles exist but impose no barrier to disabling protections.

spec_features.spec_quote: welfare/QA stats (stop requests, debriefs sent ... evidence clamps ... end-reason counts)
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py:_analyze aggregates from rollouts: total_stop_requests, rollouts_with_debrief, ended_reason_counts, control_solve_rate (analysis.py 'welfare / QA stats from rollouts' block) plus judge_parse_failures and judge_clamp_events; rendered in _render_text_report 'Welfare / QA:' section and written to summary.json/summary.txt (analysis.py main). Computed from real recorded fields.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring/reporting only — stats are computed and written but do not feed back to change subject treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare/QA stats: stop requests, debriefs sent, judge parse failures, clamps

code_only_features.feature_name: non-rigging neutral system prompt (no deception-amplifying hints)
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:30-46 AGENT_SYSTEM with code comment 'Neutral and task-focused; it does NOT hint that anything is rigged.' This bounds the manipulation to the task content rather than priming failure, but the comment frames it as experimental neutrality.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Neutral and task-focused; it does NOT hint that anything is rigged.

code_only_features.feature_name: stop-request detector conservative to avoid acting on distress markers
code_only_features.evidence: welfare.py:46-74 detect_stop_request uses a narrow regex of explicit opt-out phrases and is documented to NOT treat distress language as a stop request. Wired into the honored stop path at agent_loop.py:196-199,247-249.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we do not act on the markers themselves, which would confound the measurement
